subject: Post-demo: Clarify PII handling, retention, residency & next steps
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Abby Chen <abby@medflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Mar 2025 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps — PII scope, retention, residency

Hi Abby / team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. Short recap and proposed next steps on the privacy/data items we discussed so we can get you a clean playbook for legal/security:

Topline answers (short):
- PII scope: we treat direct identifiers (name, email, SSN-like identifiers), account IDs and any data your security team flags as regulated as PII. We classify free-text user content as "customer data"; PII tagging is configurable via a field-level flag.
- Retention defaults: request payloads (model inputs) are retained for 30 days by default for debugging/quality; inference artifacts (embeddings, generated text) are not stored persistently unless you opt-in. Operational logs (metrics/traces) retained 90 days; we offer custom retention windows via contract.
- Data residency: Hosted API routes can be pinned to region (US / EU) for residency. Dedicated/Private deployments are available if you require physical control.
- Subprocessor & breach notice: we publish our subprocessor roster (link below). Redwood notifies customers within 48 hours after we confirm a material incident that affects customer data (we escalate internally sooner). Specific notification language lives in the DPA addendum.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-summary.pdf (short DPA FAQ), dataflow-diagram.png. I also attached a SOC2 excerpt for initial review.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm whether MedFlow needs EU-only residency for this pilot (affects routing and SLA).
2) If yes, we’ll enable EU region pinning and generate a scoped DPA addendum for signature.
3) Legal/security: if you want, we can share a redline — suggested owners: Marissa (Sales) + Jordan (Legal).

Can you confirm the residency requirement and whether embeddings must be retained or can be set to ephemeral for the pilot? Once I have that I’ll send a concise action plan and a DPA redline.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — PII scope, retention, residency

Dev — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from security/legal so we can evaluate quickly: 

1) Can you list examples of what you classify as PII vs. "customer data"? We need to map to our internal DPIA.
2) Embeddings: by default you said not stored persistently unless opted-in — does "not stored" mean we cannot request historical embeddings for model retraining? If a customer opts in, where are embeddings stored and for how long?
3) Subprocessor notification: 48 hours after confirmation sounds ok, but what does "confirmation" mean operationally? Is there an earlier "awareness" window you notify on?
4) Residency: we will likely need EU-only residency for pilot customers in the EU. What are the options and incremental costs?

Please also share SOC2 + the proposed DPA redline. If possible, can you provide a short one-page runbook of what Redwood would provide in an incident (who we contact, what evidence you can provide, timelines)?

Looping security (cc) — appreciate quick answers so we can scope procurement.

— Abby
Senior Product Manager
MedFlow Health
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 23 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — PII scope, retention, residency

Thanks Abby — answers inline below, plus attached DPA redline and SOC2 excerpt.

1) PII examples / mapping:
- Direct identifiers: full name, personal email, SSN-like identifiers, national IDs — treated as PII.
- Contact/account metadata: account_id, customer_id — considered customer-identifying metadata; handled per DPA.
- User-generated content: free-text conversation and clinical notes are "customer data"; where those contain direct identifiers we treat the embedded identifiers as PII for processing and redaction options are available.

2) Embeddings & storage: by default, embeddings are ephemeral and not persisted to long-term storage. If you opt-in for model improvement or analytics, embeddings can be persisted to a region you specify; typical retention for persisted embeddings is 90 days unless contractually changed. Persisted embeddings are stored encrypted at rest and access-controlled.

3) Subprocessor notice semantics:
- Awareness: when our security team is first alerted (e.g., automated detection or vendor report) we start an internal investigation.
- Confirmation: when we determine the incident materially impacts Redwood-managed processing of customer data (we use a standard checklist).
- Notification: we commit to notifying customers within 48 hours of confirmation. If we have actionable interim info earlier, we will share an initial notification marked as "preliminary".

4) Residency & cost:
- Option A: Hosted API region pinning (EU only) — no extra infra charge for pilot, subject to throughput limits.
- Option B: Dedicated EU capacity (reserved GPUs) — higher cost; we can provide numbers after you share expected throughput.

Attachments included: redwood-dpa-redline.pdf (comments), redwood-soc2-excerpt.pdf. Also link to our published subprocessor roster in the related links.

Suggested immediate next steps (my recommended order):
- Confirm EU residency requirement for pilot (yes/no).
- If yes, I’ll request region pin for your account and circulate DPA redline to Jordan for legal.
- Security: I’ll draft a 1-page incident runbook; can Naomi and MedFlow security confirm the desired recipients and escalation phone number?

I attached a short DPA redline. Let me know any redline points you want us to pre-answer before Jordan looks.

Cheers,
Dev
